findings_to_judge.finding: IFC's fund ALAC filed a fresh Form 144 on 2026-09-01 to sell a further 857,362 LSAK shares (exactly the Rule 144 1%-of-outstanding cap, ~10.3x the baseline 20-day ADV of 83,297) starting 2026-09-02 through J.P. Morgan, after selling 857,362 shares between 2026-06-08 and 2026-08-07 and 808,737 shares between 2026-03-05 and 2026-04-17 — i.e. the seller was capped out and absent from the tape from 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-01 and returns to it in the same week as the print.

Nine-month FY2026 GAAP net loss attributable to Lesaka is -$461 thousand (nine months to 2026-03-31, per the company's own Q3 statement of operations), so management's repeated promise of 'the first year we will be profitable since the creation of Lesaka four years ago' rests entirely on Q4 FY26 clearing +$0.46m — in the quarter that carries the 30 June annual goodwill impairment test on R3,532,856 thousand (~$207m) of goodwill against $186.6m of total equity.

Management pre-committed on the 2026-05-07 Q3 call that tonight's release carries FY2027 guidance plus a first-ever three-year medium-term outlook 'inclusive of Bank Zero' — but Bank Zero is still unclosed (long-stop extended 2026-06-11 from 2026-08-06 to 2027-01-31 with Prudential Authority and exchange-control consents outstanding, and no completion 8-K on EDGAR as of 2026-09-09), it issues ~12% of Lesaka's fully diluted shares plus up to R91m cash, and Lesaka's own framing is that Bank Zero only becomes profitable in the fiscal year AFTER completion.
